summary: Emergency room visit in Vancouver for a flare-up of COPD
story: I have COPD and I manage it carefully, which is why I paid extra for the waiver when I bought this policy. On August 13 in Vancouver the wildfire smoke got bad and by the evening I could not catch my breath even with my inhaler. I went to the emergency room, where they gave me nebulizer treatments and steroids and kept me for a few hours until my breathing settled. The bill came to $780. The hospital's record and the bill are attached.

items.description: Emergency room visit, nebulizer treatments and medication

documents.name: Emergency department record
documents.content: Burrard General Hospital, Vancouver, emergency department, August 13, 2026. Patient: Harold Benson, age 68. Known COPD, diagnosed 2017, on tiotropium and a salbutamol inhaler. Reports his physician added a steroid inhaler in May 2026 after a winter exacerbation. Presented with worsening shortness of breath during a regional wildfire smoke advisory. Diagnosis: acute exacerbation of COPD. Treated with nebulized bronchodilators and oral prednisone. Observed for 4 hours, improved, discharged with a 5 day course of prednisone.

documents.name: Hospital bill
documents.content: Burrard General Hospital, August 13, 2026. Non-resident emergency department fee: $620.00. Nebulizer treatments and medication: $160.00. Total paid: $780.00.
